This repository contains a mixed C++/Python research application. Use these focused instructions to make edits, run builds, and navigate the codebase efficiently.

1) Big picture
- **Core C++ engine:** `cpp/` contains the performance-critical code (headers in `cpp/include/`, implementations in `cpp/src/`, and the build entry in `cpp/projects/main/`). Key modules: `codec` (L2 binary decode/encode), `features` (feature engineering and storage), `worker` (multithreaded workers), and `gui` (ImGui UI + coroutine infra).
- **Python glue & tooling:** `py/` supplies build scripts and utilities. `py/main.py` is the canonical C++ build script. `run.py` is a convenience entrypoint that sets run modes, invokes the Python build script, then runs the compiled binary.
- **Data/config:** runtime configuration and small data samples live under `config/` (see `config/config.json` and `config/sample/`). Documentation summary is in `doc/README.md`.

2) How to build & run (concrete commands)
- Build only (produces `cpp/projects/main/build` and `cpp/compile_commands.json` for clangd):
  - Linux/macOS (requires `cmake`, `ninja`, `clang`):
    ```bash
    # toggles available: TSAN_MODE, DEBUG_MODE, PROFILE_MODE, ASSERT_MODE (ON/OFF)
    TSAN_MODE=OFF DEBUG_MODE=OFF PROFILE_MODE=OFF ASSERT_MODE=ON python3 py/main.py
    ```
  - Windows: the same `py/main.py` chooses `clang-cl` + Ninja automatically when run on Windows.
- Build + run (high level):
  - From repo root simply run:
    ```bash
    python3 run.py
    ```
  - `run.py` sets mode flags at top of the file. It calls the same `py/main.py` build script and then runs the binary produced at `cpp/projects/main/build/bin/app_main` (or `app_main.exe` on Windows).
- Manual CMake alternative (if editing `CMakeLists.txt`):
  ```bash
  cd cpp/projects/main
  cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
  cmake --build build --parallel
  ```

3) Mode flags and debug/profiling
- The Python build script reads environment variables: `TSAN_MODE`, `DEBUG_MODE`, `PROFILE_MODE`, `ASSERT_MODE`. Set them before running `py/main.py` to toggle sanitizers, debug symbols, and profiler hooks.
- `run.py` offers a quick way to pick one mode and launch the app via the `py/mode_*.py` handlers (`py/mode_debug.py`, `py/mode_profile.py`, `py/mode_tsan.py`, etc.).

4) Project-specific conventions & patterns
- Header layout: public interfaces live in `cpp/include/...` while implementations mirror those headers under `cpp/src/...` or `cpp/*` subfolders. When editing API, update both header and corresponding implementation.
- Feature/worker pattern: feature definitions are in `cpp/include/features/` (IDs, metadata). Worker implementations live under `cpp/worker/` or `cpp/include/worker/` and communicate through shared structures in `cpp/include/shared/` (e.g. `SharedData.hpp`).
- `compile_commands.json` is generated by `py/main.py` and copied to `cpp/compile_commands.json` so editor LSPs (clangd) can index the project—do not delete this file if you expect IDE features to work.

5) Important files to inspect for context and examples
- `run.py` — top-level build+run orchestration and modes.
- `py/main.py` — canonical CMake invocation and build flags (shows platform-specific compilers and options).
- `cpp/projects/main/CMakeLists.txt` — build targets, C++ standard and compile flags.
- `cpp/include/codec/binary_decoder_L2.hpp` and `cpp/include/codec/binary_encoder_L2.hpp` — examples of binary parsing/serialization patterns used across the project.
- `cpp/include/features/backend/FeatureStore.hpp` — shows how features are persisted/read (concurrency and compression patterns).
- `cpp/include/shared/SharedData.hpp` — global/shared structures and how components exchange state.
- `doc/README.md` — high-level architecture diagram and quick map of the important directories.

6) Editor & tooling tips
- Ensure `clang`, `cmake`, and `ninja` are installed for C++ development. The build expects `clang++` on Linux/macOS by default.
- After building with `py/main.py`, open `cpp/compile_commands.json` from `cpp/` in your editor root so clangd/IDE can resolve symbols.

7) How to propose changes as a PR (developer workflow)
- For C++ changes: create a branch, run the `py/main.py` build to confirm the build succeeds, and include a small test or runtime smoke-check when possible (run `cpp/projects/main/build/bin/app_main` if it is quick). Attach `compile_commands.json` is not necessary — the build script will produce it.
- For Python tooling changes: run the script directly with `python3` and include sample inputs (config files in `config/`) in your PR description.

If anything here is unclear or you want more examples (e.g., typical patch for a feature change, where to add unit tests, or how to run the GUI headless), tell me which area to expand and I will iterate.
